statement.p: Fill in the missing values in the table given if you know that dy/dt=0.8 y. Assume the rate of growth given by dy/dt is approximately constant over each unit time interval and that the initial value of y is 10.

static.solution:
t=0 the value of y is 10. Since we are told that dy/dt=0.8 y, we know that at time t=0 the derivative of y is 0.8 (10) = 8. Thus as t goes from 0 to 1, y will increase by 8, so at t=1, y=10 + 8 = 18.
Likewise, at t=1, we get {dy}/{dt} = 0.8 (18)=14.4 so that at t=2, we obtain y=18 + 14.4 = 32.4.
At t=2, we have dy/dt=0.8 (32.4)=25.92 so that at t=3, we obtain y=32.4 + 25.92 = 58.32.
Continuing similarly, dy/dt|_{t=3} = 46.656, so that at t=4 we have y = 58.32 + 46.656 = 104.976.
